newsitem.title: USA: Dow surges to record as stocks stage broad rally.
newsitem.headline: Dow surges to record as stocks stage broad rally.

text.p: Wall Street stocks staged a broad rally on Monday, powering blue chips to a new all-time closing high.
The Dow industrials surged 79 points to close unofficially at 7079, eclipsing their old record of 7067.46, set on February 18.

Analysts said several of the bull market's hallmarks were in display throughout the session, first in the mutual fund inflows that continue to lift blue chips and second in the bargain hunting that helped tech stocks shake off their woes.

According to industry tracking firm Mutual Fund Trim Tab, cash inflows to U.S. stock mutual funds totalled $1.49 billion for the three-day period ended March 6, versus $7 million for the two days ended March 3.
As in the past, analysts said, mutual fund managers appeared to be pouring their newfound cash directly into the top tier stocks.
"It looks like the big boys are back buying the big stocks," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
In a departure from recent sessions, however, investors seemed to be sifting through the beleaguered tech sector, looking for bargains created by the group's recent sell-off.
"People are nibbling away at some of these stocks," said Arnie Owen, director of equity trading at Kaufman Brothers.
"Some of these stocks have corrected 30 or 40 percent and whenever you get a situation like that, that's when you start to see bargain hunting."
But with Nasdaq well off its record highs and buying interest still focused on large caps, analysts shied away from predicting stocks were poised for a new spurt higher.
"I don't think we're at the rally stage yet," said Barbara Marcin, vice president at Citibank Global Asset Management. "This looks like it could be a little bit of index chasing."
Several analysts also noted that the gains came on fairly light volume, a condition that will have to change before they are convinced of the market's conviction.
"If this new high were accompanied by stronger volume, it might be a signal we're ready to pop the cork," Ackerman said.
Consumer non-cyclicals were among the Dow's strongest components, with Procter & Gamble Co up 4-1/4 to 124-3/4 and Philip Morris Cos Inc up 2-3/4 to 138-3/4.
Oil shares also fueled the rally. Texaco Inc rose two to 105, Exxon Corp gained 2-5/8 to 103 and Chevron Corp rose 1-1/4 to 67-3/8.
Among tech shares, Cisco Systems Inc gained two points to 53-3/8, shrugging off news that PaineWebber had downgraded the shares to neutral from buy.
Microsoft Corp gained 3-1/4 to 100 and U.S. Robotics Inc rose 2-3/8 to 58-3/4.
Office Depot Inc tumbled 5-1/2 to 17-1/8 after the Federal Trade Commission announced its opposition to the company's planned merger with Staples Inc.

The FTC said it believed a merger of companies -- two of the nation's three office products superstore chains -- would reduce or eliminate competition in several markets. Staples shares fell 1-5/16 to 23-1/4, while shares in the third chain, OfficeMax Inc edged up 1/4 to 13-1/4.
American Home Products Corp rose 1-3/8 to 68-1/8 after a medical study showed the over-the-counter anti- inflammatory drug ibuprofen could reduce the risk of developing Alzheimer's disease.
American Home Products is one of several companies that manufacture the drug. Some others include Johnson & Johnson, which gained 5/8 to 61-1/4 and Mylan Laboratories Inc, which rose 1/2 to 17-3/8.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 10.92 points to 1322.72.
The S&P 500 index rose 8.68 points to 813.65.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
